propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui Ecclesiam tuam beati Thomae Confessoris tui mira eruditione
clarificas, et sancta operatione fecundas: da nobis, quaesumus; et quae
docuit, intellectu conspicere, et quae egit, imitatione complere. Per
Dominum nostrum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Historical source s-thomae-aquino-confessoris-ecclesiae-doctoris/main/Collect/all/1; same-witness-conclusion-table. Complete petitions equal and actual Latin conclusion prefixes match the same printed family through-our-lord at passage.francis-xavier-lasance.the-new-roman-missal.benziger-revised-1945.resume-orations-conclusion-table-2026-10-23-verify; tracked rule/formula passage.francis-xavier-lasance.the-new-roman-missal.benziger-revised-1945.resume-orations-conclusion-table-2026-10-23-transcription. Actual English short cue retained literally, without expansion or response. Cross-owner reuse requires entire literal canonical Latin equality including conclusion, punctuation, wraps and final LF, SHA256 f8e33fdc7841d147dfb1ccfc51c942f859c6473574f1db2e302f4171c7c2f684. Original target proof passage.catholic-church.missale-romanum.vatican-typica-1962.temporal-s-thomae-aquino-confessoris-ecclesiae-doctoris-orations retained. No source-recipient calendar attestation or official 1962 English claimed.

translations.text: O God, Who dost enlighten Thy Church with the wondrous learning of blessed Thomas, Thy Confessor, and dost make it fruitful with his holy labors, grant us, we beseech Thee, both to understand what he taught and to imitate what he practiced. Through our Lord.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Sancti Thomae Confessoris tui atque Doctoris nobis, Domine, pia non desit
oratio: quae et munera nostra conciliet; et tuam nobis indulgentiam semper
obtineat. Per Dominum.

translations.caution: Original study translation; not approved for liturgical use or recitation.
translations.text: Lord, may the devout prayer of Saint Thomas, your Confessor and Doctor, never fail us; may it make our gifts acceptable and always obtain your pardon for us. Through the Lord.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Ut nobis, Domine, tua sacrificia dent salutem: beatus Thomas Confessor tuus
et Doctor egregius, quaesumus, precator accedat. Per Dominum nostrum.

translations.caution: Original study translation; not approved for liturgical use or recitation.
translations.text: Lord, so that your sacrifices may bring us salvation, we ask that blessed Thomas, your Confessor and eminent Doctor, come forward to intercede. Through our Lord.
